questions.question: The ________ exchange rate is the price of one unit of foreign currency in terms of domestic currency.
questions.solution: The nominal exchange rate is defined as the number of units of the domestic currency that can purchase a unit of a given foreign currency. A decrease in this variable is termed nominal appreciation of the currency.

questions.question: ________ of an input is defined as the change in output per unit of change in the input when all other inputs are held constant.
questions.solution: The marginal product of an input (factor of production) is the change in output resulting from employing one more unit of a particular input (for instance, the change in output when a firm's labor is increased from five to six units), assuming that the quantities of other inputs are kept constant.

questions.question: In Microsoft Excel, the _______() function returns the largest value among the values passed as arguments.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __MAX__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• The Microsoft Excel **MAX function** returns the** largest value from the numbers provided**. It can be used as a worksheet function (WS) in Excel. As a worksheet function, the MAX function can be entered as part of a **formula in a cell **of a worksheet.
 
• The **syntax **for the MAX function in Microsoft Excel is:
 
 
• **MAX( number1, [number2, ... number_n] )**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The MAX function **ignores empty cells**.
 
• The MAX function in current versions of Excel accepts up to **255 arguments**. If arguments contain no numbers, MAX returns 0.
 
• Arguments can be provided as **numbers, names, arrays, or references** that contain numbers.
 
• The MAX function **ignores TRUE and FALSE values**, and numbers entered as text unless they are typed directly into the list of arguments.
 
• To include logical values in a **reference**, we need to use the **MAXA function**.
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5a79c8844e003e0a712410d366dd88744d11c9dc88196b748f1f032bfa782e1c.png]

questions.question: What is the process of melting is also called?
questions.solution:
• **Melting, or fusion**, is a physical process that results in the phase transition of a substance from a solid to a liquid.
 
• This occurs when the internal energy of the solid increases, typically by the application of heat or pressure, which increases the substance's temperature to the melting point.

questions.question: Arrest of _________ in 1930 led to angry demonstrations in streets of Peshawar.
questions.solution: The Khudai Khidmatgar (literally Servants of God), led by Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, were a group of Pashtuns committed to the removal of British rule through non-violent methods. On 23 April 1930, Ghaffar Khan was arrested after giving a speech in Utmanzai urging resistance to British rule. This led to demonstrations by a cross section of civil society in and around Peshawar, led by Maulana Abdur Rahim Popalzai against discriminatory laws like the Frontier Crimes Regulation against the people of the province.

questions.question: If the mass of an object is 60 kgs, what will be its weight on the moon? (N = Newton)
questions.solution:
To find the weight of an object on the moon, you simply multiply its mass by the gravitational force of the moon.

**Explanation:**

m = 60kg; the value of gravity on moon is, g = 1.63m/s²

Therefore:

weight = mass*gravity = 60 × 1.63 = 97.8 N (approx. 100N)

questions.question: In an acid base reaction which product is produced along with a salt?
questions.solution: In a typical *acid base* neutralization the *salt* is created by the positive ion from the base and the negative ion from the acid, forming the *salt* and the hydrogen from the acid combining with the hydroxide from the base to form water.

questions.question: Taenia (Tapeworm), Fasciola (Liver fluke) are examples of which Phylum?
questions.solution: The phylum name Platyhelminthes literally means "flatworms." Members of this phylum are soft, thin-bodied, leaf or ribbon like worms, including planaria of ponds and streams, as well as the flukes and tapeworms parasitic in human and other animal bodies.

questions.question: The side mirrors of vehicles are of which type of mirrors?
questions.solution: The side mirrors of vehicles are convex mirrors. Because the image is smaller, more space can be covered by this mirror, so a convex mirror provides for a larger field of view than a plane mirror. This is why they are used whenever a mirror with a large field of view is needed. For example, the passenger-side rear view mirror on a car is convex.

questions.question: Who discovered Potassium?
questions.solution: In 1806 English chemist Sir Humphry Davy discovered that chemical bonding was electrical in nature and that he could use electricity to split substances into their basic building blocks – the chemical elements. Metallic potassium was first isolated by him using this process in 1807 through the electrolysis of molten caustic potash (KOH).

questions.question: Beyond the ________, the Himalayas bend sharply to the south and spread along the eastern boundary of India.
questions.solution: The Purvanchal Mountains cover the states of Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Tripura, Nagaland, Meghalaya and Mizoram. This range is an eastern extension of the Himalayan Range System, in north eastern India. It bends sharply to the south beyond the Dihang River gorge, and spreads along the eastern boundary of India with Myanmar.

questions.question: Where is Humayun's Tomb is located?
questions.solution: Located near the crossing of Mathura road and Lodhi road in New Delhi, this magnificent garden tomb is the first substantial example of Mughal architecture in India. It was built in 1565 A.D. nine years after the death of Humayun, by his senior widow Bega Begam.

questions.question: "Trade unions" is listed in the _________ list given in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India.
questions.solution: The Concurrent List or List-III (Seventh Schedule) is a list of 52 items given in the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India. It includes the power to be considered by both the central and state government. Trade unions; industrial and labour disputes is listed as an item in this list.

questions.question: __________ scheme launched by the Central Government aims to promote entrepreneurship among people from schedule caste/schedule tribe.

options.text: Gram Uday Se Bharat Uday Abhiyan

questions.solution: The objective of the Stand-Up India scheme is to facilitate bank loans between 10 lakh and 1 crore to at least one Scheduled Caste (SC) or Scheduled Tribe (ST) borrower and at least one woman borrower per bank branch for setting up a greenfield enterprise. Stand-Up India scheme is proposed to be operated through 1.25 lakh bank branches in the country. The loans would be specifically for SC/ST/Women entrepreneurs.

questions.question:
Which of the statements given above are correct?

1. The author of the novel 'Brave New World' is Aldous Huxley.

2. The author of the novel 'An Affair Downstairs' is Sherri Browning.

3. The author of the novel 'Darkness at Noon' is Victor LaValle.
questions.solution: The author of the novel 'Darkness at Noon' is not Victor LaValle. Darkness at Noon is a novel by Hungarian-born British novelist Arthur Koestler, first published in 1940. It is an unforgettable portrait of an aging revolutionary, Nicholas Rubashov, who is imprisoned and psychologically tortured by the very Party to which he has dedicated his life.

questions.question: __________ writ is issued by a Higher Court (High Court or Supreme Court) when a lower court has considered a case going beyond its jurisdiction.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prohibition**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Writs:

 
 
• They are issued by the Supreme Court and High Court.
 
• Purpose: for enforcement of the Fundamental rights given in Part III
 
• Articles of the Constitution- 
 
 
• Article 32 for Supreme Court
 
• Article 226 for the High court 
 
 
 
 
 
• Writ of Prohibition:
 
 
• Prohibition simply means ‘To forbid.’​
 
• This writ is issued to any inferior court, or quasi-judicial body prohibiting it from continuing the proceedings in a case, where it has no jurisdiction to try.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are five types of writs:

 
 

 
 
Habeas Corpus

 
 
 
 
• The writ is issued to produce a person who has been detained before a court and to release him if such detention is found illegal.
 
 
 
 

 
 
 Mandamus 

 
 
 
 
• This writ is issued to a lower court or public authority to perform a public or statutory duty.
 
 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
Certiorari

 
 
 
 
• This writ is issued for quashing the order already passed by an inferior court or quasi-judicial authority
 
 
 
 

 
 
Quo warranto

 
 
 
 
• This writ is issued with a view to restraining a person from holding a public office to which he is not entitled.

questions.question: To which country, India gave Rs. 35 crore rupees to children of freedom fighters in under the new ‘Muktijodha scholarship' scheme?
questions.solution: India will give Rs. 35 crore rupees to children of freedom fighters in Bangladesh under the new ‘Muktijodha scholarship’ scheme in the next five years. Under the scheme, students at higher secondary level will get a one-time grant of Tk 20,000 (Rs 15,370) and students at the undergraduate level will get a grant of Tk 50,000 (Rs 38,430).

questions.question: Which nation is not a part of the South Asian Free Trade Area?
questions.solution: China is not a part of the South Asian Free Trade Area.The South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) is the free trade arrangement of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC). The agreement came into place in 2006, succeeding the 1993 SAARC Preferential Trading Arrangement. SAFTA signatory countries are Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.

questions.question: The _________ were the successors of Timur, the ruler of Iran, Iraq and modern-day Turkey.
questions.solution: The Mughals were descendants of two great lineages of rulers. From their mother's side they were descendants of Genghis Khan, ruler of the Mongol tribes. From their father's side they were the successors of Timur, the ruler of Iran, Iraq and modern-day Turkey.

questions.question: In the names Mangifera indica (mango), Solanum tuberosum (potato) and Panthera leo (lion), the terms Mangifera, Solanum and Panthera represent the higher level of?
questions.solution: In Mangifera indica(mango), Solanum tuberosum (potato) and Panthera leo (lion) all the three names, indica, tuberosum and leo, represent the specific epithets, while the first words Mangifera, Solanum and Panthera are genera and represent another higher level of taxon or category.
